style: who is speaking to whom, and what has just happened

candidates.angle: Achuta, the unerring one, is asked to drive
Hrishikesha, the master of the senses, is asked to stop
Arjuna asks to see the men before fighting
candidates.evidence: देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किनकिन के साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है

angle_hi: अच्युत, जो कभी न डिगने वाले हों

en.intro: Arjuna has raised his bow, but now he stops. He asks his charioteer to turn the chariot and show him the men on the field.
en.notice: Arjuna calls out to Achyuta, the unerring one, and asks him to place the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the men he must battle.
en.next: Arjuna then asks Krishna to stop the chariot so he can see the men standing there, eager for battle.
en.meaning: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war.

hi.intro: अर्जुन ने अपना धनुष उठा लिया है, लेकिन अब वे रुक जाते हैं। वे अपने सारथी से रथ घुमाने और उन्हें मैदान के लोगों को दिखाने के लिए कहते हैं।
hi.meaning: संजय बताते हैं कि हे राजन, तब अर्जुन ने श्रीकृष्ण से यह वचन कहा: हे अच्युत, मेरे रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में खड़ा कीजिए।
hi.notice: अर्जुन अच्युत, यानी जो कभी न डिगने वाले हों, को पुकारते हैं और उनसे रथ दोनों सेनाओं के बीच में रखने को कहते हैं ताकि वे उन लोगों को देख सकें जिनके साथ उन्हें युद्ध करना है।
hi.next: अर्जुन फिर श्रीकृष्ण से कहते हैं कि वे रथ को रोक दें ताकि वे वहाँ खड़े हुए उन लोगों को देख सकें जो युद्ध के लिए आए हैं।

en.intro: Arjuna has raised his bow, but now he stops. He asks his charioteer to turn the chariot and show him the men on the field.
en.body: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war. Arjuna calls out to Achyuta, the unerring one, and asks him to place the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the men he must battle. Arjuna then asks Krishna to stop the chariot so he can see the men standing there, eager for battle.

issues: meaning_changed: "Arjuna calls his charioteer Hrishikesha, the master of the senses, and then asks him to place the chariot between the two armies so he can look at the men he must kill." (The notice claims Arjuna calls Krishna 'Hrishikesha' in this verse, but the Sanskrit source only has 'अच्युत' (Achyuta). The word 'हृषीकेशं' is in the dative case ('to Hrishikesha') as part of the sentence structure, not as a direct address (vocative) by Arjuna. Additionally, the source does not explicitly state that Arjuna wants to look at 'the men he must kill' (जिनको उन्हें मारना है); it only says he wants to see 'with whom I must battle' (किनकिन के साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है).)

unsupported: "Arjuna then asks Krishna to stop the chariot so he can see exactly who has come to fight him." (The phrase 'exactly' (बिल्कुल/ठीक से) is an unsupported factual claim. The source text simply says he wants to look at them (देख न लूँ); it does not specify the degree of exactness or precision of his observation.)
